back: The rate when the labour market is in equilibrium (no cyclical unemployment); also the rate at which inflation is stable (NAIRU).
No disequilibrium (cyclical) unemployment; frictional and structural unemployment remain.

front: What is the difference between equilibrium and disequilibrium unemployment?
back: Equilibrium: frictional, structural and voluntary unemployment when the market clears. Disequilibrium: excess supply of labour from a wage above equilibrium or low demand.

front: What is **hysteresis** in the labour market?
back: The natural rate rises after a long period of high actual unemployment, because skills and contacts are lost.
Voluntary: people choose not to work at the going wage. Involuntary: willing and able to work at the going wage but cannot find a job.

front: Name two barriers to geographical mobility of labour.
back: Housing costs and family ties (also lack of information and the cost of moving).
Demand-side policy: raise aggregate demand through lower interest rates, higher spending or lower taxes.
Supply-side policies: training, retraining, mobility support, job information and regional policy.

front: What happens if demand is expanded when unemployment is at the natural rate?
back: Inflation rises with little fall in unemployment.
